subject: Mutual Action Plan: POC environment readiness — follow-up & clarifications
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alexis Porter <alexis.porter@gridlytics.com>, Sam Todd <sam.todd@gridlytics.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Mutual Action Plan: POC environment readiness — follow-up & clarifications

Hi Alexis / Sam,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on scope. Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the POC environment setup we discussed (VPC peering, IP allowlists, SSO/SAML, secrets/KMS). I pulled together milestones, tentative owners, and the dependencies we heard from your side.

High level summary:
- Target POC start: Feb 7, 2027 (target close for initial evaluation: Feb 28)
- Infrastructure gate for us: VPC peering + IP allowlist + routing confirmation
- Identity gate for us: SAML/IdP test user + metadata exchange + assertion test
- Secrets gate: KMS access pattern + secret rotation/process note

Please review the attached MAP (redwood_map_v1.pdf) and the network requirements spreadsheet. Two quick asks to help us finalize the plan:
1) Can you confirm which team will own VPC peering on your side and an expected contact?
2) Can you provide the public CIDR ranges you intend to use for egress or the IPs you can allowlist?
3) Any compliance constraints around key management (bring-your-own-key vs. us-managed)?

I've looped in Jordan for post-sales coordination. Karthik, can you review the KMS/secret note and flag any additional questions the infra team will need?

Next step: If Alexis can reply with the items above by Friday (1/15), we'll update the MAP and propose firm milestone dates.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Attachments:
- redwood_map_v1.pdf (PDF)
- network_requirements_table.xlsx (Excel)
From: Alexis Porter <alexis.porter@gridlytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Todd <sam.todd@gridlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 11:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: POC environment readiness — follow-up & clarifications

Ben — thanks for the doc and the clear asks. Quick answers from our side below (see inline):

On Tue, Jan 12, 2027 at 09:02 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> 1) Can you confirm which team will own VPC peering on your side and an expected contact?

We own the peering from our cloud infra team. Primary contact: Sam Todd (cc'd). Sam will kick off the peering request — ETA to open the ticket: tomorrow (1/13).

> 2) Can you provide the public CIDR ranges you intend to use for egress or the IPs you can allowlist?

We can provide a stable set of outgoing IPs for the POC. Preliminary ranges (subject to change once infra ticket is acted on):
- 35.198.64.0/24
- 34.82.128.0/25
I will confirm the final list in the peering ticket. If you need single IPs for allowlisting we can reserve them and share — let us know how many you need.

> 3) Any compliance constraints around key management (bring-your-own-key vs. us-managed)?

We prefer BYOK but can accept Redwood-managed keys for a short POC window. For production we will require BYOK and an audit trail. I'll flag the procurement/compliance owners after the peering ticket is open.

Couple of additional notes from Sam: we have a SAML IdP (Azure AD) and can provide metadata and a test account. Sam, can you share the metadata URL and a test user by EOD 1/14?

Thanks — Alexis
Alexis Porter
Head of Platform | Gridlytics

Attachments: none
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Todd <sam.todd@gridlytics.com>, Alexis Porter <alexis.porter@gridlytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 13:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: POC environment readiness — follow-up & clarifications

Thanks Alexis — that's great. Sam — appreciate you owning the peering. A couple of follow-ups from our infra/security checklist (cc'ing Karthik):

- For allowlist: if you can reserve 3 public IPs and share them, that will simplify firewall rules on our side for the POC control plane.
- For SAML: metadata URL + a test account with email sam.test@gridlytics.com would be ideal; we'll run an assertion test against our staging SP.
- For KMS: Karthik, Gridlytics indicated BYOK preference. Can you call out the minimum information we need from their KMS team (roles/policies, key id format, rotation window) so they can include it in the ticket?

Karthik replies below (internal):

> From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
> Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 13:48:00 -08:00
>
> Ben / Sam / Alexis —
>
> Quick list for KMS/BYOK to help us plan:
> 1) Key ID (ARN or provider-specific identifier) and the permission model (which IAM principals can decrypt).
> 2) Whether Gridlytics will allow the Redwood runtime principal to perform decrypts, or whether we should integrate via a proxy. For POC, cross-account decrypt with an explicit role is fine.
> 3) Rotation cadence (months) and whether there is an API for key rotation events (webhook or CloudTrail logs).
> 4) For secrets (DB creds, API keys), a short example of the retrieval flow (SDK calls or HTTP endpoint) so we can script provisioning for the POC.
>
> If Sam can provide the SAML metadata URL and the reserved IPs by EOD 1/14, we can lock milestone dates and I'll produce a short infra runbook for the POC by 1/18.
>
> — Karthik

Ben
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Alexis Porter <alexis.porter@gridlytics.com>, Sam Todd <sam.todd@gridlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 15:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: POC environment readiness — follow-up & clarifications

Looping back with a proposed timeline based on the dependencies called out:

- 1/14: Gridlytics opens peering ticket + shares SAML metadata + reserved IPs (owner: Gridlytics / Sam)
- 1/18: Redwood infra delivers POC runbook (owner: Karthik) — includes test accounts, allowlist steps, and KMS integration notes
- 1/22: Peering and firewall rules validated end-to-end (owners: Gridlytics infra + Redwood infra)
- 2/07: POC ramp begins (test prompts, throughput profiling)
- 2/28: POC evaluation complete — decision checkpoint (success criteria and pass/fail in MAP)

Action items: 
- Sam: confirm metadata URL + share reserved IPs (due 1/14)
- Karthik: draft runbook (due 1/18)
- Ben: update MAP with firm dates and share final version after Sam's reply

If everyone agrees, I'll update the MAP and the HubSpot deal with these milestone dates.

Best,
Jordan
Principal Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
